_trafficRecomputeTicksSource: FEAT-2326609798 inc5 r2 (Lead amendment 1, BUG-877, 2026-09-10): placeholder cadence, balance regime - webconsole/src/sim/engine.ts advance() refreshes SimState.trafficSnapshot (the commute/gridlock/emergency wellbeing inputs) only every N ticks (or on the first advance() when the snapshot is absent), never per-tick; a full traffic assignment on the tick hot path measured 96x (7.6ms -> 728ms at 20,000 buildings, BUG-877). 30 ticks is an unvalidated placeholder pending Aaron's balance pass, not a perf-tuned value.
_disclosure: GR#15: V/C volume-delay curve parameters (BPR alpha/beta) and lane capacities are data-driven here. bprAlpha/bprBeta must be finite and strictly positive -- LoadConfig rejects zero, negative, or NaN values fail-closed (MOD-023 r2 destructive verdict).

_webconsoleMetresPerTileSource: Lead amendment (Bev, 2026-09-09, FEAT-2326609796 inc3 BOW comment): the WEBCONSOLE grid tile is 50 m, per webconsole/src/sim/debugjson.ts:1249 (grid.tileMetres:50) and data.ts:1759-1760 (road costs 'rebased onto this game's 50m tile'). This is DISTINCT from the ENGINE cell (data/georef.json cellSizeM: 10, the OS Terrain 50 raster) -- do not conflate the two; the Go engine.traffic BPR maths uses cellSizeM, never this field.
_maxAttributionRadiusTilesSource: BUG-847 rework (2026-09-09): caps webconsole/src/sim/trafficDemand.ts's nearestSegmentWeights multi-source BFS radius so cost is bounded by the MAP (grid.ts MAP_W=624 x MAP_H=368, max possible Manhattan diameter 992 tiles) and this figure, never by the city's own occupied bounding-box diameter -- the BUG-847 finding measured 5.12M BFS ops from ONE 400-tile-distant outpost building because the old radius WAS the bbox diameter. 250 tiles = 12.5km at webconsoleMetresPerTile's 50m/tile, a generous upper bound on any plausible road/rail catchment for this game's city scale (the OS Terrain 50 Folkestone start tile is a fraction of that); tiles further than this from every segment of a class report as UNATTRIBUTED demand (forecastUnattributedOf) rather than being silently dropped or paying the old unbounded flood cost.
_nearestSourceForTilesOpsFallbackThresho: BUG-935 r3 rework (2026-09-11, closing BUG-967 P1 -- the r2 round found the r2 rework's 150,000,000 figure was ABOVE the real crossover, so a mid-size DENSE-ROAD-NETWORK city took the primitive branch and was 2.5-4.5x SLOWER than HEAD's own flood). r3 re-measured on deterministic grid fixtures (roads on a 1-in-5 row/column lattice, the same adversarial dense-network shape the r2 round used) with the primitive vs boundedNearestSourceMapOf isolated (9 reps, JIT-warmed, first 2 dropped) at radius 250: 3,294,225 ops (55x55, 1,089 sources x 3,025 queries) 9.75ms vs 68.44ms flood (primitive 0.14x, faster); 29,160,000 ops (120x75, 3,240 x 9,000) 78.47ms vs 88.41ms (0.89x, still marginally faster but close); 70,726,500 ops (150x93, 5,070 x 13,950) 262.16ms vs 163.47ms (1.60x, SLOWER); 105,267,600 ops (180x95) 451.91ms vs 245.12ms (1.84x, SLOWER); 144,000,000 ops (200x100, matches the r2 round's own fixture) 786.42ms vs 225.12ms (3.49x, SLOWER, consistent with the round's 3.08x finding); 909,941,760 ops (~224x224, 50k buildings) 341.36ms vs 284.41ms (1.20x, SLOWER but small in absolute terms). The real crossover on this adversarial shape sits between 29.16M (still ~faster) and 70.7M (already 1.6x slower) -- an order of magnitude under the old 150,000,000 figure and consistent with the r2 round's own 29.16M/144M findings. 20,000,000 ships with real margin BELOW even the favourable 29.16M point, so every measured city size from 9k buildings upward takes the flood branch (byte-identical to HEAD, no regression -- end-to-end computeTrafficSnapshot A/B against a threshold=1 HEAD-equivalent run, fresh state per rep so no memo-hit contamination, showed the r3 threshold matching or beating the HEAD-equivalent run at every size from 9k to 50k, all differences within run-to-run noise) while a genuinely small city (well under 20,000,000 ops -- the actual BUG-935 production scenario of a fixed ~1,248-2,591-tile infra network plus a handful of player buildings) still gets the primitive's real speedup. Author-suite pin (attack-bug935-round.test.mjs) asserts this shipped value is <= 30,000,000 (BUG-967's own bar). Unvalidated placeholder pending a real perf-CI gate at this scale, like every other measured-not-derived figure in this file.
